title: Mint-debt hook ignores BalancerPoolerV2 pool address changes — debt keeps accruing against orphaned-backing dispatcher state
rejection_reason: Design simplicity is intentional. The trigger is an onlyOwner action (setPool), and the PO has deliberately chosen loose hook↔dispatcher coupling over complex relationship checking, accepting the "little extra phUSD minted" tradeoff. Per C4 known-invalid rules this is a reckless-admin/centralization pattern, not an exploitable vulnerability — no attacker path exists without admin misoperation. All four proposed mitigations add exactly the coupling the PO is avoiding.
description:
The hook's `dispatcher` is `immutable` — set once at construction to the BalancerPoolerV2 instance that will call `onDispatch`. The hook has NO reference to the Balancer pool; it does not track which sUSDS/phUSD pool is currently backing the debt. But `BalancerPoolerV2._pool` is mutable via `setPool(newPool)` (line 84-87). This creates three distinct failure modes for the debt↔backing invariant:

1. Owner calls `setPool(newPool)` while previous-pool BPT is still held by the dispatcher. Prior-round finding M-03 showed this strands previous-pool BPT for `withdrawBPT`, but also: new dispatches flow into the new pool, while `mintDebt` still contains accruals whose original backing was on the old pool. The hook pulls mint debt via `phUSD.mint(recipient, debt)` without any check that the pool currently bound to the dispatcher is the one that actually received the USDS that generated that debt line item.

2. `pool()` is owner-gated (authorized pooler) and may never be called between dispatches and the next `setPool`, so freshly dispatched sUSDS may sit on the dispatcher and never enter the pool at all. The hook still accrues full debt on every dispatch as if backing exists.

3. The hook silently allows debt to outrun backing. The recipient can call `pull()` at any time to mint phUSD against a debt ledger that includes entries for which the corresponding sUSDS either (a) is still unpooled on the dispatcher, (b) entered a previous pool now stranded, or (c) entered the current pool but at a materially different price than at dispatch time.

This is a cross-contract economic invariant: the hook's debt ledger is only meaningful when paired with the specific pool that holds the corresponding sUSDS LP position. Nothing in the code binds them.
impact: Debt can be collected via `pull()` without any assurance that equivalent value is actually sitting in the pool the protocol is using to back NFT holders. Owner-triggered pool rotation directly desynchronises the two sides. After a pool rotation plus a `pull()`, minted phUSD exists against accounting that doesn't correspond to the current backing position — concretely, recipient holds phUSD that can be dumped into the new pool, extracting sUSDS that was deposited by users whose NFT claim is now backed by less-than-`(1-ratio)%` of their nominal USDS contribution.
attack_path: Users dispatch a total of Y USDS over many mints; hook accrues Y*ratio/100 phUSD debt.
Owner calls `BalancerPoolerV2.setPool(newPool)` — debt ledger is unchanged, new pool has zero protocol BPT.
Users continue minting on the new pool; hook debt grows further.
Recipient calls `pull()`. All accumulated phUSD debt is minted in one go.
Recipient dumps that phUSD into whichever sUSDS/phUSD pool is liquid (current or prior) — the drain occurs on real users' sUSDS regardless of which pool the hook notionally 'backed'.
recommendation: Couple the hook to a specific pool, not just a specific dispatcher. Two viable shapes: (1) store `pool` on the hook at construction and have the hook read back `BalancerPoolerV2.pool()` on every dispatch and revert if it has changed, forcing the owner to deploy a new hook + settle via `pull()` before rotating pools; or (2) automatically force-settle (i.e. zero out `mintDebt` and emit an event) whenever a pool rotation is detected. In either case, `BalancerPoolerV2.setPool` should be gated on `mintDebt == 0` on the bound hook (or require the owner to pull first). Currently the two contracts know about each other one-way (hook → dispatcher immutable) but the pool address sits entirely in the dispatcher with no observer.
